# `silk/semver/version`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Semantic versions: strict SemVer 2.0.0 parsing, precedence, and display.

## When to use

Use [`Version.parse`](#Version.impl.parse) to read a version such as `1.4.0-beta.2+build.7`, and compare versions with
`<`, `==`, or [`Version.comparePrecedence`](#Version.impl.comparePrecedence). To test a version against a requirement such as
`^1.2` or `>=1.0.0, <2.0.0`, use `silk.semver.range`.

## Details

A [`Version`](#Version) holds the three numbers as `u64` values and borrows the pre-release and build text
from the parsed input. Parsing does not allocate. The parser accepts exactly the grammar of
SemVer 2.0.0: no `v` prefix, no spaces, and no leading zeros in numbers.

Precedence follows SemVer 2.0.0: numbers compare numerically, a pre-release version is lower than
its release, and build metadata does not change precedence. `==` and `<` also compare build
metadata after precedence, so two versions are equal only if their text is the same.

## Gotchas

`1.0.0+a` and `1.0.0+b` have the same precedence, but `==` returns `false` for them. Use
[`Version.comparePrecedence`](#Version.impl.comparePrecedence) to compare versions as SemVer 2.0.0 does.

## Examples

### Find the newer of two versions

```silk
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.semver.version { Version, SemverError }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let release = match Version.parse("1.4.0") {
    Result<Version, SemverError>.Success { value } => value
    Result<Version, SemverError>.Failure { error: _ } => { return 1 }
  }
  let beta = match Version.parse("1.4.0-beta.2+build.7") {
    Result<Version, SemverError>.Success { value } => value
    Result<Version, SemverError>.Failure { error: _ } => { return 1 }
  }
  if !(&beta < &release) || beta.prerelease != "beta.2" || beta.build != "build.7" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

## See also

[Semantic Versioning 2.0.0](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html) defines the grammar and the
precedence rules.

Import as `Version` with `import silk.semver.version { Version }`.

<a id="Version"></a>

## `Version`

```silk
pub struct Version<'text>
```

A semantic version, `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` with an optional pre-release and build metadata.

### Details

The pre-release and build fields borrow the text that was parsed, without the `-` or `+`. They
are empty when the version has none. The value is `Copy` and cannot live longer than its text.

`==` and `<` compare precedence first and then build metadata, so `==` is `true` only for
versions with the same text. Build identifiers compare in the same way as pre-release
identifiers.

### Gotchas

A value made with a struct literal is not checked. Use [`Version.parse`](#Version.impl.parse) or [`Version.make`](#Version.impl.make) to
get a valid version.

<a id="Version.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub fn parse(text: string<'text>) -> Result<Version<'text>, SemverError>
```

Parses a SemVer 2.0.0 version, such as `1.4.0-beta.2+build.7`.

#### Details

The text must be exactly `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, then optionally `-` and dot-separated
pre-release identifiers, then optionally `+` and dot-separated build identifiers. Identifiers
use ASCII letters, digits, and `-`. A number fits in `u64`. The result borrows `text`. Nothing
is allocated.

#### Errors

- `SemverError` with the reason and the byte offset of the first problem:
  - `Empty` for empty text.
  - `UnexpectedEnd` if a part is missing, as in `1.2`.
  - `UnexpectedCharacter` for a byte that is not valid there, as the `v` of `v1.2.3`.
  - `LeadingZero` for a number or numeric pre-release identifier such as `01`.
  - `NumberTooLarge` for a number above 18446744073709551615.
  - `EmptyIdentifier` for an empty identifier, as in `1.2.3-` or `1.2.3+a..b`.

#### Gotchas

Leading and trailing spaces and a `v` prefix are errors. Version requirements accept a `v`
prefix, but versions do not.

<a id="Version.impl.comparePrecedence"></a>

### Associated function `comparePrecedence`

```silk
pub fn comparePrecedence(left: &Version<'_>, right: &Version<'_>) -> Ordering
```

Compares the SemVer 2.0.0 precedence of two versions. Build metadata does not count.

#### Details

The major, minor, and patch numbers compare numerically, in that order. Then a version without
a pre-release is greater than one with a pre-release. Pre-release identifiers compare one at a
time from the left: numeric identifiers compare as numbers, other identifiers compare by ASCII
byte order, and a numeric identifier is lower than a non-numeric one. If all shared
identifiers are equal, the version with more identifiers is greater. So
`1.0.0-alpha < 1.0.0-alpha.1 < 1.0.0-beta < 1.0.0-beta.2 < 1.0.0-beta.11 < 1.0.0`.

#### Gotchas

`1.0.0+a` and `1.0.0+b` have `Equal` precedence, but `==` on them returns `false` because `==`
also compares build metadata.

<a id="Version.impl.nextMajor"></a>

### Method `nextMajor`

```silk
pub fn nextMajor(self: &Self) -> Version<'static>
```

Returns the next major release: `major + 1` with `0.0`, or the same numbers for a pre-release
of `X.0.0`.

#### Details

The result has no pre-release and no build metadata. `1.4.2` becomes `2.0.0`, and
`2.0.0-rc.1` becomes `2.0.0`, because `2.0.0` is the release that `2.0.0-rc.1` comes before.

#### Gotchas

The program traps if the major number is 18446744073709551615 and must increase.

<a id="Version.impl.nextMinor"></a>

### Method `nextMinor`

```silk
pub fn nextMinor(self: &Self) -> Version<'static>
```

Returns the next minor release: `minor + 1` with patch 0, or the same numbers for a
pre-release of `X.Y.0`.

#### Details

The result has no pre-release and no build metadata. `1.4.2` becomes `1.5.0`, and
`1.5.0-rc.1` becomes `1.5.0`.

#### Gotchas

The program traps if the minor number is 18446744073709551615 and must increase.

<a id="Version.impl.nextPatch"></a>

### Method `nextPatch`

```silk
pub fn nextPatch(self: &Self) -> Version<'static>
```

Returns the next patch release: `patch + 1`, or the same numbers for a pre-release.

#### Details

The result has no pre-release and no build metadata. `1.4.2` becomes `1.4.3`, and
`1.4.3-rc.1` becomes `1.4.3`.

#### Gotchas

The program traps if the patch number is 18446744073709551615 and must increase.
